personal.name: Syed Burhan Ahmed
personal.title: AI Engineer, Researcher & Technical Mentor
personal.tagline: AI Engineer specializing in Computer Vision, Agentic Systems & Production ML
personal.bio: Building production ML systems with Python, PyTorch, FastAPI, LangChain, and n8n. At OptimusFox, shipped a production recommendation engine and an AI vendor-search chatbot. Built InsightVision, an on-device-first vision-language surveillance platform combining zero-shot detection, Kalman-filter tracking, and Gemma-4 OCR at ~11.5GB peak VRAM on a single GPU. Engineered a domain-specific MoE expert-pruning pipeline that delivered a measured 10.51× inference speedup on Gemma-4-26B. IEEE published author (ICIC 2025).
personal.closingBio: Open to collaborating on challenging, impact-driven engineering problems. Whether it's deployable computer vision systems, workflow automation infrastructures, or mentoring developers, the focus is on building reliable tech that solves real-world bottlenecks.
story: I'm an AI Engineer building production-grade systems across Computer Vision, Agentic AI, and applied ML — from recommendation engines and vendor-search chatbots at OptimusFox to research on vision-language models and detection-and-tracking pipelines at UMT's AVR Makerspace Lab. My first IEEE paper covered vision-based fall detection for elderly surveillance, and beyond engineering, I've trained 120+ participants as a Generative AI Master Trainer and mentored student and graduate interns across multiple cohorts.

I'm drawn to problems where research meets deployment — the kind of work that has to actually run in production, not just in a notebook. Open to collaborating on deployable CV systems, workflow automation, or mentoring developers who want to build reliable tech that solves real bottlenecks.

experience.title: AI Researcher – Computer Vision & Robotics
experience.company: AVR Research Group Makerspace Lab, UMT
experience.description: Served as a research assistant conducting applied VLM benchmarking, hybrid vision-pipeline architecture design, and downstream model optimization — spanning early benchmarking work through building InsightVision, an on-device vision-language surveillance platform, and a domain-specific MoE expert-pruning pipeline for deployment on consumer GPU hardware.
achievements: Benchmarked closed-source vs. open-source VLMs (Gemma 4, Grounding DINO, CLIP, Jina) against human baselines on perception tasks — object counting, license plate recognition, scene understanding — on a constrained 16GB GPU.

Designed and built out a hybrid detection-and-tracking architecture (Grounding DINO + BoT-SORT, SAM3 + BoT-SORT, standalone SAM3) into InsightVision, a fully on-device FastAPI microservice with Gemma 4 handling OCR and prompt-driven natural-language querying, running at ~11.5GB peak VRAM on a single GPU.

Engineered a domain-specific MoE expert-pruning pipeline for InsightVision's vision/OCR workload, achieving a measured 10.51× inference speedup on Gemma-4-26B-A4B and enabling full on-GPU residency on a single 16GB VRAM card.

projects.title: InsightVision
projects.subtitle: Offline AI Video Surveillance & Semantic Search Platform
projects.description: A fully offline AI video surveillance platform developed as my undergraduate capstone project, orchestrating a hybrid detection-and-tracking pipeline (Grounding DINO + BoT-SORT, SAM3 + BoT-SORT, and standalone SAM3) with Gemma 4 handling OCR (~443ms) and prompt-driven querying, running real-time tracking at ~7.7 FPS within ~11.5GB peak VRAM on a single GPU. Delivered as a FastAPI microservice with a React 'Cyber-Ops' dashboard and Redis-backed state, developed under UMT's AVR Research Group.
projects.longDescription: Built out over a continuous AVR Research Group engagement (Jul 2025 – Aug 2026): began with initial architecture research and VLM benchmarking, developed through UMT's Capstone-I/II sequence to a final capstone defense in July 2026, then further optimized via a follow-on MoE expert-pruning project. Backend architecture and system documentation were finalized ahead of the defense, with the frontend deployed on Vercel and backend deployment via Tailscale Funnel/Cloudflare Tunnel.

projects.title: Freak AI
projects.subtitle: Memory-Augmented Conversational Agent
projects.description: A rule-based conversational agent modeling five human-inspired memory systems (social, semantic, PAM, episodic, sensory) as a live Neo4j knowledge graph, with real-time D3.js dashboards visualizing memory formation. Combines AIML pattern matching with Prolog fact reasoning, plus an optional Alexa-style ESP32 voice interface with DHT11 sensor logging for spoken interaction.

projects.title: Voice-Based Smart Attendance System
projects.subtitle: IoT-Driven Attendance Platform
projects.description: Built the ESP32 control hub for a dual-mode attendance system: passive NFC + fingerprint verification for daily attendance, and a voice-driven admin mode for student enrollment. Captured audio via a MAX9814 mic, sent it to a Flask speech-to-text server over HTTP, and routed the returned keyword (enroll/update/delete/scan) to trigger the matching action — with DFPlayer Mini audio prompts and OLED status feedback throughout.

projects.title: ArUcoNav: Autonomous Vision-Guided Robot
projects.subtitle: Real-time pose estimation & dynamic path planning
projects.description: Co-engineered an autonomous navigation stack (Python + OpenCV) using ArUco marker pose estimation, after a rival color-tracking approach failed under venue lighting on demo day. Diagnosed and fixed an inverted heading-vector bug through manual vector-math debugging, then implemented dynamic 'Safety Node' routing via Euclidean distance to steer around obstacles. Deployed on ESP32 with PID steering correction for a clean 13-second finish.
